chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them, upon them be peace:
Regarding a man who buys a female slave or marries her, not for maturity (rushed/impulsive), and takes her for himself, he said: 'If he does not fear the defect upon himself, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying or marrying a female slave without maturity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the validity of acquiring a female slave or marrying her when the buyer or husband acts without full maturity or caution (ghayr rashida). The ruling hinges on the absence of hidden defects ('ayb) that would impose a liability or loss upon the acquirer, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that such transactions remain valid provided no specific detriment is incurred. This highlights the practical flexibility in personal status law regarding capacity and defect inspection in pre-modern Islamic societies.
